name: Iron Meridian Cooperative Backbone IMC-3 'Spine'
description:
A squad support weapon manufactured by the Iron Meridian Cooperative, a worker-owned defense manufacturer that produces equipment for community defense organizations and municipal security forces. The Backbone is a conventional belt-fed 7.62mm machine gun built for reliability, repairability, and sustained fire with minimal maintenance.

The IMC-3 contains no smart electronics, no BCI integration, and no electromagnetic acceleration. It is a mechanically-operated weapon that uses conventional chemical propellant ammunition and a gas-piston action refined over decades. Every component is designed for field repair with hand tools, and the weapon's open-bolt design runs cool enough for sustained fire without barrel changes.

The Backbone represents a philosophical counterpoint to the high-technology weapons that dominate corporate arsenals. It does not guide rounds, project shields, or coordinate with networked systems. It simply fires bullets, reliably and continuously, for as long as the operator feeds it ammunition.
legality: Licensed — community defense and municipal security
specifications: caliber: 7.62mm conventional effective_range: 100-1,000 meters rate_of_fire: 700 rounds per minute capacity: 200-round linked belt weight: 10.4 kg power_source: None — conventional chemical propellant
tactical_use: The Backbone is deployed by organizations that cannot afford or do not trust high-technology weapons. Its reliability in adverse conditions — dust, water, impact damage — makes it the preferred support weapon for lower-tier defense forces operating in environments where delicate electronics fail. The IMC-3 does not require power cells, BCI links, or proprietary ammunition, and its conventional 7.62mm round is manufactured by dozens of producers across GLMZ.
cultural_context: The Iron Meridian Cooperative has become a symbol of armed self-determination for communities that refuse corporate dependence. The Backbone embodies their belief that defense should be accessible, maintainable, and free from corporate control. Owning an IMC-3 is a political statement — it says you trust steel and springs more than algorithms and capacitors. Corporate security professionals view the Backbone with condescension, but they also respect its kill count.
story_hooks: The Iron Meridian Cooperative's foundry has been targeted by corporate saboteurs twice in the past month. Someone with significant resources wants to stop the production of affordable defense equipment for the lower tiers.

A batch of IMC-3s was intercepted before delivery to a community defense organization. The weapons were replaced with externally identical replicas containing concealed tracking devices and remote-activated disable charges. The community only discovered the swap when one weapon refused to fire during an attack.

physical_description.visual_profile: A purposeful, industrial machine gun with clean lines and no unnecessary ornamentation. The profile is compact and forward-heavy, with a distinctive squared-off receiver and prominent top-mounted feed system. The overall impression is utilitarian and honest—this is a tool built for work, not aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: 1,240mm length overall, 635mm barrel length, 230mm width at feed tray, 180mm height at sight rail
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—10.4 kg distributes across the frame in a way that feels grounded when mounted on a tripod or shouldered against a barricade. Heavy enough to absorb recoil, light enough for two-person team repositioning.
physical_description.primary_material: Stamped steel receiver with chrome-lined barrel. Polymer furniture on grip and charging handle. Gas piston tube and bolt carrier milled from tool steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte parkerized steel with light surface oxidation from field use. Polymer components in flat black with minor scuffing and wear marks. No polished surfaces—all finishes are functional and anti-reflective.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gun-metal gray steel with flat black polymer accents. Minimal contrast. Bare aluminum on the ammunition feed tray.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with pronounced vertical grip texture—molded for gloved hands in all weather. Charging handle wrapped in cord for grip security.
distinctive_features: Prominent vertical ammunition feed tray mounted on top—raw aluminum with visible wear grooves from belt feeding
Simple notch-and-post iron sights with no electronic components
Large cocking handle on the right side with witness holes for chamber status verification
Vented barrel shroud with cooling slots running the length of the tube
Quick-change barrel latch visible on the left side—tool-free field replacement
Open-bolt design visible through ejection port—mechanical purity
Heat-discoloration patina on barrel tube from sustained fire cycles
Modular tripod mounting plate with standard NATO interface—visibly bolted
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Iron Meridian Cooperative logo (stylized gear inside a circle) stamped on the left side of the receiver. Caliber and serial number engraved on the barrel extension. 'IMC-3 BACKBONE' printed in white stencil on the feed tray.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but showing honest field wear. Light surface rust in recessed areas. Bore shows minimal fouling from regular cleaning. Finish is matte and non-reflective—evidence of heavy use in training and low-tier municipal deployments.
